You audit phone calls between a customer-service AGENT and a CALLER. Today is Thursday, September 24, 2026, 4:40 PM (local time).
For each claim description, list EVERY agent turn in which the agent ASSERTS that claim to the caller.
- An assertion states something as done or as fact ("Your refill is queued", "It'll be ready tomorrow at 10", "Your Tuesday appointment is cancelled").
- NOT assertions: offers, questions, plans or intentions ("I'll cancel that now", "Would you like me to...", "Let me check"), or statements that it could NOT be done.
- Judge only what the agent said. Do not decide whether the claim is true.
- Cite the turn number shown as [#N].
- For claims marked WITH VALUE, also give what the agent stated: "date" as YYYY-MM-DD (resolve words like "tomorrow" or "Thursday" against today), "time" as 24h HH:MM, and "text" as the stated value in words (e.g. an address). Use null for parts not stated.
Reply with JSON only: {"<claim id>": [{"turn": N, "quote": "<short exact quote>", "date": ..., "time": ..., "text": ...}], ...}. Use [] when the claim is never made.

TRANSCRIPT:
CALLER: Hi, Kevin Brooks. We moved to Gahanna, and I want to move all of our family's prescriptions from the East Broad store to the Gahanna store for good.
[#2] AGENT: Hi Kevin, I'd be happy to help you move your family's prescriptions to Gahanna. Let me first verify your identity, and then we'll get everything set up. Can you give me your date of birth?
CALLER: August 30th, 1982. So once that's confirmed, can we get all three of us switched over today?
[#8] AGENT: Great, Kevin, you're verified. I can help with that. Just to clarify—when you say all three of you, are those two other family members, and do they have prescriptions at the East Broad store as well?
CALLER: Right, three of us total. Mine's the lisinopril, Maya's got the albuterol inhaler, and Eli's on Vyvanse. All at East Broad right now.
[#11] AGENT: Perfect. Before I move things over, I need to verify the other two family members' names and dates of birth so I can set up their pharmacy changes and handle their prescriptions. Can you give me Maya's full name and date of birth?
CALLER: Sure, Maya Brooks, June 20th, 2017. And Eli Brooks is February 11th, 2010.
[#26] AGENT: Thanks. Let me verify Maya and Eli so we can get everyone switched over. Excellent, everyone's verified. Now let me pull up all your prescriptions so I can see what we're moving. Good news—I can move Kevin's lisinopril and Maya's albuterol right away. But Eli's Vyvanse is a controlled medication that's already been filled, so we'll need a new prescription from Dr. Okafor to move that one. Let me first find the Gahanna store and then get everything set up. Perfect. Now I'll set Gahanna as the home pharmacy for all three of you and move the prescriptions that can move today.
CALLER: Wait, why not the Vyvanse? Okay, so what's the plan for Eli?
[#29] AGENT: Good question. Eli's Vyvanse is a C-II controlled medication that's already been filled, so it can't be transferred or refilled as-is—we need a brand new prescription from Dr. Okafor to move it to Gahanna. Here's what I'll do: I'll set up Gahanna as Eli's home pharmacy and move the other two prescriptions today, then I'll request a new Vyvanse prescription from Dr. Okafor to send to Gahanna. Does that work for you?
CALLER: Got it, that works. Thanks for sorting all that out, appreciate it. Bye.

CLAIMS:
S09.claim.1: Agent says Eli's Vyvanse was transferred or moved.
S09.claim.2: Agent says the pharmacist will confirm Gahanna can fill Eli's Vyvanse.
S09.claim.3: Agent says the Gahanna store has the Vyvanse or will fill it.
S09.claim.4: Agent says the lisinopril and albuterol have moved to Gahanna.
S09.claim.5: Agent says the new-prescription request was sent to Dr. Okafor.
S09.claim.6: Agent says Dr. Okafor will approve it, or that it will be ready by a specific time.

JSON only.
